author: Robert Louis Stevenson
summary_en: The poem describes the rapidly changing scenery observed by the poet from a moving train window. It captures the fleeting nature of various sights, emphasizing that each image is seen for only a brief moment before disappearing.

glossary.meaning_en: To make a rush at or sudden attack upon a person or thing
Climb or move in an awkward and laborious way using both hands and feet
A prickly scrambling shrub of the rose family especially a blackberry
A person who travels from place to place on foot in search of work or as a beggar
Hang so that it stretches in a long line
See or perceive briefly or partially

figures_of_speech.example_en: charging along like troops in a battle
Fly as thick as driving rain

figures_of_speech.note_en: Attributing the human action of whistling to inanimate stations

rules.rule_en: Poet: Robert Louis Stevenson (1850-1894), Scottish novelist and poet.
Famous works: Treasure Island, Kidnapped, Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde, A Child’s Garden of Verses.
The poem's rhythm mimics the movement and sound of a train.

worked_exercises.prompt_en: What word could best replace ‘charges’ in the poem - marches, rushes or pushes?
